## What is available now

The published development release is
[0.4.0-preview.1](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.1).
The [install guide](install.qmd) deliberately still installs that version.
The WSL preview already installed is also the older preview. A source-code change
does not update an installed command.

The next development preview is being prepared. Its version, source commit and
download commands must be filled in from the reviewed release before publication.
This page does not create a tag, change the package version or replace a binary.

## What the next preview is intended to add

| Change | What it means when the candidate is released |
|---|---|
| Keep one project context | A child command keeps the selected project, configuration and run version when a script changes folder. |
| Separate trial results from released files | Generated-output path queries default to a folder under the selected cache for that run's version. A successful production build can copy declared results to their final folders. |
| Use familiar working folders | Scripts inherit the folder from which the build was launched; document tools keep their native rules. An explicit project-folder option remains available. |
| Control output cleanup | The default keeps other final output files. You can opt into clearing immediately before analysis or after successful analysis. Preview does not clear released outputs. Document-output replacement has its own documented rules. |
| Handle R package data explicitly | output-r-data resolves to the project's data folder for final lookup. Only an explicit declaration, or a normalized legacy data declaration, opts that folder into ordinary build management. |
| Share supported HTML reports | Individual Quarto/R Markdown HTML and modeled Quarto projects default to embedding resources when unspecified. Explicit and inherited false values remain respected. |
| See useful results and failures | The acceptance fixtures produce a CSV and an HTML report, preserve prior final/archive bytes on preview or supported failure, and return structured success/failure results. Git credentials are not required for these local workflows. |

The selected R/Python/report example has a verified order. A renderer can handle
several documents as one project; this does not promise arbitrary mixed-language
targets always execute one by one in the order written.

## Limits that stay in place

- The existing R package and its helpers are unchanged. The acceptance examples
  call the CLI through small test adapters; they do not prove RStudio, Knit or
  direct R API parity.
- Bookdown's site renderer keeps its native resource policy. This slice does
  not add its embedding fallback. Do not treat its linked site as a portable
  single-file HTML report.
- Individual rendering still rejects unsupported inherited/external metadata
  and unsupported layouts. Quarto project metadata remains a separate supported
  path; nested Quarto projects are rejected.
- Project fallback requires modeled text inputs and temporarily prepares only
  unspecified HTML options. It restores original source bytes. Changing a prepared
  source or native input set before rendering is rejected; other input types need
  explicit renderer embedding settings.
- Explicitly nonembedded HTML may need its original resources. Literal Markdown
  and LaTeX references keep their native meaning; no resource URLs are rewritten.
- Preview recovery covers recorded managed paths. It does not isolate arbitrary
  script effects, handle every concurrent change, or provide crash/power-loss
  atomicity.
- Complete provenance, durable attempt/release records, analysis-free publication
  retry and M2 remain unfinished.
- Delivery remains Linux/WSL and Windows x86-64. macOS/ARM binaries are not supplied.

Use sample data or an independently backed-up disposable copy while evaluating
this development preview. Read the [build reference](cli/build.qmd) and
[lifecycle](lifecycle.qmd) before production use.

## Review status and evidence

The [source PRs](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pulls) record exact heads,
remote runs and downloadable evidence. R-data is merged. Embedding and combined
acceptance corrections still require independent clearance and a final run on
the integrated tree. Branch preparation artifacts are supporting evidence, not
proof that the installed preview or final candidate contains every change.

## Final integrated acceptance

1. Finish independent review and integrate the source slices, then the acceptance
   driver. Record the exact resulting source commit. Resolve documentation and
   workflow overlaps without changing reviewed behavior; report any new head.
2. Run the existing pinned-image workflow on that exact integrated tree. Require
   complete locked Rust regressions, documentation examples, warning-free API
   documentation, actual R/Python/rendering acceptance and the combined M1 driver.
   Retain host-platform, installer and website checks and the existing native-browser
   documentation witness.
3. Inspect the JSON and downloadable files from both acceptance drivers. Confirm
   configured/no-init and actual local directory initialization; ordered
   Python/R/report steps; computed CSV value 84; four relocated embedded reports;
   structured deliberate failures; unchanged prior ordinary generated-output/archive
   bytes under none; prior docs preserved on preview/failure and replaced on
   successful document finalization; and exactly two expected-role local archive
   manifests for each successful production case, with object bytes matching the
   CSV/report witnesses and index/manifests identifying release1.2.4. Require the
   final project VERSION to be next-dev1.2.4.1.
   Preview/failure cases must create no archive manifests. Require the corruption
   probes, immediate init-directory checks and failing Git-call witness as well.
4. Require the R-data undeclared/explicit/legacy activation matrix and embedding
   unspecified/explicit/inherited-false matrix on the same integrated source.
   A previous green branch is supporting evidence, not a substitute.
5. Reconcile the website's behavior, feature and compatibility descriptions with
   the actual supported CLI behavior and deferred limits. Record independent
   clearance before release work advances.

These steps do not close M1 by themselves. The final report must identify the
accepted scope, exact integrated source and remaining limits.

## Release and WSL installation sequence

1. Prepare a separate reviewed version change. Cargo.toml and the root package
   entry in Cargo.lock must agree. The CLI package version is distinct from an
   analysis project's VERSION; do not change users' project versions.
2. Prepare release notes for the chosen version and exact source. Keep the
   public README/install download commands and downloaded-binary documentation
   checks pinned to the currently published preview.1 throughout tagging, draft
   asset checks and publication. Their CI fetches public downloads and
   source-commit.txt, so an unpublished pin cannot pass those checks.
3. Only after the source/version gates pass, tag the exact reviewed commit and
   run the existing preview release workflow. It creates a draft prerelease.
   Inspect both actual platform assets, source-commit.txt, version.txt and the
   exact checksum entries. Run the remote binary and installer checks.
4. Publish only the verified draft, then confirm public downloads match the
   checked assets. Only after public-byte verification, make a separate
   post-publication documentation change updating README/install pins, version
   wording, source-commit links and downloaded-binary check expectations together.
   Run those public-download checks before merging that documentation change.
   Keep the instructions in plain language, with platform/deferred limits visible;
   never silently substitute GitHub's older stable Latest.
5. Inside WSL Ubuntu, preserve the previous user-local binary, download the
   explicit published version, verify its checksum and install into the existing
   user-writable directory. No local Rust compilation, administrator access or
   persistent authentication changes are needed. Do not disturb thesis containers,
   the existing R package or the Windows Codex process.
6. Check the installed binary by its full path for version, help and machine
   capabilities, then run a tiny disposable configured preview and deliberate
   failure. Confirm the shell resolves the expected command. Record the actual
   installed version and verification evidence before saying installation is done.

No release, tag or local binary replacement is made by this documentation preparation.
